rows.medi_said: أنا سمعت / متأخر اليوم. صحيت. That's right.
rows.why: He said سمعت (I heard) for 'I woke up'; her صحيت at 07:06 lands inside his line and he repeats it with "That's right" (GR-24).
تأخر (to be late, verb/noun) used where the adjective متأخر is needed; she only types it in chat and re-says متأخر 80 s later while prompting him on, so not a clear voiced fix.
Clock time needs el-; her whole reply was الـ and he fixed it to على العشرة (GR-25).

rows.medi_said: Okay أنا شوي-- أنا كان قنيش شوي--
rows.why: kaan must take the I-ending with ana; she recast أنا كنت and he repeated it.

rows.amal_said: We never say هذا الصبح just say الصبح or بالصباح.
rows.why: He said 'this morning' with a demonstrative (08:23, again 08:54/08:58); she said we never say it that way.
rows.english: I was a bit lazy this morning.
rows.proposed_rule: 'This morning' is just el-subu7 or bel-subu7, never hada/hadi el-subu7 (Amal: 'We never say هذا الصبح').

rows.medi_said: أنا لا مش شجاع اليوم. مش شجاع اليوم.
rows.why: شجاع means brave; she recast متشجع (sheet: motivated | Mitshajje3 | متشجع).
laazem went straight to a noun; she supplied the verb 'you should take' and he said أنا لازم أخد عطلة (GR-27).
rows.english: I need to take a vacation.

rows.medi_said: أنا لازم أخد عطلة وسفر، سفر.
rows.why: He used the noun سفر where the verb أسافر is needed; she rephrased in English 'I should travel' and he said لازم أسافر (PG-22).
خطط takes la-; she prompted 'You plan for' and he tried لا سفر (la-safar).

rows.medi_said: بس أنا راح آآآ على آآآ عموي.
rows.why: ra7 needs a verb after it; she asked 'What's going?' and he said راح أروح.
rows.english: But I'm going to go to my uncle's.

rows.amal_said: Either على or عند which one؟ Can't put two.
rows.why: He stacked two prepositions (على + عند); she said you can't put two.
He invented عموي for 'my uncle'; she recast عمي twice and he said That's right.

rows.amal_said: No. It's the whole-- It's the reason of our whole one month long lesson.
rows.why: For 'we will have fun' he tried 'bida'; she said No and hinted until he produced ننبسط.

rows.medi_said: Tesh-teshki? Tesh-- Was it tesh-- What was it?
rows.why: He forgot camping and asked; she hinted خيمة then gave تخييم (sheet: camping | ta5yeem | تخييم) - a didn't-know.

rows.amal_said: Yes. بس we learned how to say الأول for a feminine. What is it? Do you remember?
rows.why: ساعة is feminine so the adjective must be الأولى; she prompted and he produced الساعة الأولى.

rows.medi_said: and التاني الساعة means a different hour.
rows.amal_said: لا. We can't say تاني الساعة. It doesn't mean anything.
rows.why: He put el-taani before the noun; she said it means nothing (taani before a noun never takes el-). Said while working out the rule, so low.

rows.chat: el-masari ra7 yiju fi tani youm
rows.why: She had just told him مصاري is plural but he used the singular verb يجي; only her chat writes yiju, so let pass.
rows.english: The money will come on the second day.

rows.amal_said: مم، مم، هذي اليوم. مرة، هذي المرة.
rows.chat: hadi el-marra el-tania illi bashufek elyoam
rows.why: He said اليوم (day) instead of المرة (time); she echoed his هذي اليوم then said هذي المرة and he rebuilt المرة التانية.
rows.english: This is the second time (I see you today).

rows.medi_said: So ساعة الأول-- It should be ساعة الأول.
rows.chat: awal el-sa3a = the beginning of the hour
rows.why: Noun lacks el- while the adjective has it, and the adjective is masculine; she recast الساعة الأولى (the A8 part repeats the 18:12 row).
Listening: أول اليوم (awal before el-noun) is 'the beginning of the day'; she repeated it laughing until he said 'The beginning of the day'.

rows.medi_said: الأول اليوم. ... The beginning of the day. ... الأول اليوم.
rows.why: He put el- on أول in the 'beginning of' construction; she said it means nothing and gave اليوم الأول / أول اليوم.
Adjective has el- so the noun needs it too; she recast المرة الأخيرة. (His أخر -> أخيرة was a self-fix.)
Listening: بيجي is present; he translated it as past and she said 'To come'.
Repeating her phrase he dropped el- on the adjective; she recast الأخيرة.

rows.medi_said: هي ال، الختيارة ال أول. Is it awwal?
rows.why: Feminine noun ختيارة needs الأولى; she supplied it.
rows.english: She is the first old woman in our program.

rows.amal_said: تاني حدا would mean the second person.
rows.why: For 'someone else' taani must come after the noun; before it means 'second'. She explained and he accepted.

rows.medi_said: Oh, you're right. Uh, هذا الثاني.
rows.amal_said: حدا التاني is no. X. Just حدا تاني.
rows.why: Engine wrote هذا الثاني; her echo shows he said حدا التاني - 'someone else' takes no el-; she said no, just حدا تاني.

rows.amal_said: عشر y. / y عشر not عشرة.
rows.why: 3-10 before a plural drop the -a: عشر دقايق; she said عشر not عشرة.
آخر is the tool form; the adjective is أخير. Her ال أخي- and his الأخير are at the same second, so it may be a self-fix.
Plural دقايق takes أخيرات per her; he gave masculine singular أخير.

rows.medi_said: you say it was dwarf? What was it again?
rows.why: He asked for guests again after she introduced ضيف/ضيوف; didn't-know.

rows.chat: ana basoo2 nafs el-taree2 kul yom
rows.why: طريقة is way/method (sheet: way / method | Tariqa | طريقة); for route she gave طريق (sheet: road / way / route | 6ariq | طريق) and he said نفس الطريق.
rows.english: I drive the same route every day.

rows.why: He put نفس after the noun with من; she prompted 'مش نفس...' and he said مش نفس الإشي.
rows.english: The rule for ghair is not the same thing.
rows.proposed_rule: nafs goes BEFORE the noun and the noun takes el-: nafs el-ishi, never ishi min nafs (Amal: 'نفس always takes ال after').
